etymologies.etymologyHTML: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ὁρμῶν (hormôn), present participle of ὁρμάω (hormáō, “to set in motion, to urge on”), from ὁρμή (hormḗ, “rapid motion forwards, onrush, onset, assault, impulse to do a thing, effort”).

definitions.definition: (physiology) Any substance produced by one tissue and conveyed by the bloodstream to another to effect physiological activity.

quote.citation: 1998, Paul Valent, Trauma and fulfillment therapy: a wholist framework:
quote.text: Interfemale dominance may be facilitated by female sex hormones as well as adrenal testosterone...

quote.citation: 2019, Bill Bryson, The Body: A Guide for Occupants, Black Swan (2020), page 165:
quote.text: Hormones are the bicycle couriers of the body, delivering chemical messages all around the teeming metropolis that is you.

definitions.definition: (LGBTQ, colloquial, usually in the plural) Sex hormones, as used in hormone replacement therapy for transgender or intersex people.
(pharmacology) A synthetic compound with the same activity.

quote.citation: 1962, D. J. B. Ashley, Human Intersex:
quote.text: Tumours of the adrenal cortex which secreted feminizing hormones  […]

quote.citation: 2021, Jane Y. Xu, Michelle A. O’Connell, Lauren Notini, Ada S. Cheung, Sav Zwickl, Ken C. Pang, “Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators: A Potential Option For Non-Binary Gender-Affirming Hormonal Care?”, in Front Endocrinol, →DOI:
quote.text: Gender-affirming hormone therapy may involve testosterone for trans people assigned female at birth (AFAB) and estradiol and anti-androgens for trans people AMAB.
